stem.en: You find an unlabelled microscope slide of a single-celled organism. It has a well-defined nucleus and many cilia. Which kingdom does it most likely belong to?

text.en: Protista: one cell, a true nucleus, and cilia.

feedback.en: Yes. Paramecium is a protist of this kind, and cilia are how it moves.

text.en: Monera: a single cell that moves by itself.

feedback.en: Monera cells have no true nucleus, and this cell has one.

text.en: Fungi: a single cell, in the same way as yeast.

feedback.en: One cell does not make a fungus. Yeast has a chitin wall and does not move with cilia.

text.en: Plantae: a cell with a well-defined nucleus.

feedback.en: Plants are multicellular, and this organism is a single cell.

explanation.en: A single cell with a true nucleus is a unicellular eukaryote, and cilia are found in protists such as Paramecium. Monera has no true nucleus, and plants are multicellular.

hints.en: First ask whether it is a prokaryote or a eukaryote.
